newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah stronger in slow late trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah stronger in slow late trading.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was stronger against the dollar in slow late trading on Monday due to offshore buying, dealers said.
One U.S. bank dealer said offshore players seemed to remain upbeat on the rupiah despite relatively ample supply.
He said the dollar-rupiah rate was trapped in a range between 2,324 and 2,326 in the morning, but the rupiah edged up against the dollar in the afternoon on offshore buying.
He said this might be due to the high yield offered by the rupiah, coupled with a robust economy and low inflation.
Spot rupiah was quoted at 2,322.2/23.2 at 0900 GMT against 2,323.5/24.5 at the opening.
One Japanese bank dealer said some operators were also seen unloading short-dated swap rates which also caused longer-term swap rates to follow the down trend in the afternoon.
Dealers said a stabilised money market liquidity from last Friday seemed to have aided short-dated swap rates to fall.
They said overall sentiment on the rupiah remained firm.
Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,322.75/23.25 and 2,323.25/23.75, respectively.
Overnight swap was at 0.40/0.45 and tom/next at 0.33/0.40.
One-month swap was quoted 14.00/15.00, two at 30.00/32.00, three at 46.50/47.50 and six at 96.50/97.00 points.
Bank Indonesia raised its intervention rate by one point to 2,310/2,502 and the conversion rate also by one point to 2,310/2,358 on Monday.
The rupiah has risen steadily against the dollar since the central bank widened its intervention band to eight percent from five percent last Wednesday.
